content:
incident-bot: ALERT: Spike in tail latency and 503s on cont-batch pool: gpu-pool-9. Metric: cont_batch_p99_latency up 6x, error_rate 4.8% (rolling 5m). Suspected: KV cache paging + very large batches. Links: http://grafana/redwood/d/contbatch

alex.m: noticing correlated OOM paging on nodes in zone-us-east1-b, logs showing heavy KV eviction churn.

priya.s: oncall takeover — I'm looking. @alex.m what's the current max_num_seqs and max_batch_tokens for this pool?

alex.m: config shows: max_num_seqs=64, max_batch_tokens=65536, continuous_batch_timeout_ms=200. Those numbers look accidentally permissive after last rollout.

megan.sre: wow 64 seqs is huge for long-context requests. That would explode KV cache pressure. Paging observed in dmesg on node-7.

tom.runtime: confirm: our runtime keeps per-batch KV cache entries ~sum(seq_len) across seqs. With 64 seqs and some requests at 8k tokens, we hit host swap threshold.

priya.s: impact estimate? jordan.cs can you surface affected customers?

jordan.cs: two enterprise customers in prod on that pool showing elevated latency and occasional 503s (approx 8% of their requests failing during peak). They're being notified.

kris.ops: I'm ready to do a config patch, suggest a quick mitigation plan: 1) temporarily disable continuous batching for pool gpu-pool-9 OR 2) reduce max_num_seqs to 4 and max_batch_tokens to 16384 and increase timeout to 400ms. Which route?

alex.m: disabling cont-batch might drop throughput but will stop the big batch formation immediately. Greener quick fix: set max_num_seqs=4 and max_batch_tokens=16384 as a hotfix then observe.

priya.s: agree. Rollout plan: patch pool config, apply to pool, scale restart serving processes on affected nodes if required. Deploy via config service with canary to 2 nodes first.

priya.s: hotfix command (config-service):
```bash
cfgctl set pool gpu-pool-9 max_num_seqs=4 max_batch_tokens=16384 continuous_batch_timeout_ms=400 --dry-run=false
```

kris.ops: executing canary now on node-7 and node-8. Will watch for 2 minutes.

deploy-bot: cfgctl apply started by kris.ops for pool gpu-pool-9; canary nodes: node-7,node-8; change id: cfg-202003.

alex.m: logs show immediate reduction in batch sizes from median 48->3 seqs. KV eviction rate down 85%.

megan.sre: nice. latency p99 dropping back toward baseline. error_rate down to 0.9% on canary.

kris.ops: promoting rollout to remaining nodes.

deploy-bot: cfgctl apply promoted; remaining nodes rollout in progress.

priya.s: while we roll, also enable ephemeral tracing for a subset of affected customers to verify no quality regressions. jordan.cs can you toggle?

jordan.cs: toggled tracing for customer ids CUST-443 and CUST-991, streaming key outputs to secure bucket.

tom.runtime: suggestion for post-incident root cause: recent config templating change in autoscaler added a default max_num_seqs of 64 for pools with throughput>100qps. That default shouldn't apply to long-context pools.

alex.m: I'll open a PR to change the default and add a safety cap. Also will add a validation that max_batch_tokens <= 32768 unless explicitly overridden by an opt-in flag.

megan.sre: quick observation: we still see a small tail of elevated latency on node-3 — looks like a remaining large KV object from earlier. Planning a rolling restart of serving processes on node-3 in 5m. Any objections?

priya.s: go ahead. coordinate with kris.ops.

kris.ops: restarting serving on node-3 now.

deploy-bot: process restart on node-3 initiated.

priya.s: customer impact summary for postmortem: - Root cause: continuous batching config defaults + missing validation -> oversized batches -> KV cache thrash + host paging. - Impact: 2 enterprise customers experienced up to 8% request failures during peak windows; platform-wide p99 latency up to 6x for ~18 minutes. - Mitigation: immediate config hotfix (max_num_seqs=4, max_batch_tokens=16384, timeout increased) + rolling restarts and cache stabilization. - Long-term fixes: config validation, safer defaults, alert for KV eviction rate > threshold, and add auto-fallback to disable cont-batching on high paging.

jordan.cs: customers acknowledged, one requested ETA for full mitigation — gave them 30m and status page update.

alex.m: monitoring shows metrics back to normal. Will keep thread open for 24h for any regression.

priya.s: filing postmortem now. tagging eng-runtime and eng-sre. Thanks all. :tada:
